/**

 */
const NON_INDEXABLE_FIELD_OPERATORS = new Set([
  '$ne',
  '$nin',
  '$regex',
  '$not',
  '$elemMatch', // Complex to optimize
  '$all', // Complex to optimize
  '$size', // Cannot use index
  '$type', // Cannot use index efficiently
  '$mod', // Cannot use index

  '$geoIntersects',

text: { "answer": "MangoDB indexes work by creating in-memory data structures that store document references by their _id for efficient lookup. For equality lookups, indexes use a Map<serializedKeyValue, Set<documentIdString>>, and for range queries, indexes use a sorted array of { value, docIds } for single-field indexes. Indexes are built lazily on first query after documents are loaded, and the system checks if a field condition can use an index, returning the type of usage: 'equality', 'range', or null if not indexable. Queries use indexes for simple equality conditions, the $eq operator, and $in with single value which is effectively equality, as well as range operators. However, queries cannot use indexes efficiently with operators like $ne, $nin, $regex, $not, $elemMatch, $all, $size, $type, $mod, $geoWithin, $geoIntersects, $near, and $nearSphere, and certain query operators like $or, $nor, $not, $text, $where, $expr, and $jsonSchema force a full collection scan." }
